title: Transactional swap plane with backpressure smoothing and progressive cutover anchors
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: production rollouts that perform a direct model swap frequently spike latency or trigger circuit breakers when the target model has transient queuing behavior or different KV cache warmup characteristics. This PR introduces a transactional swap plane that performs a staged, atomic handoff at the request-routing layer with an integrated backpressure-smoothing controller and progressive cutover anchors per-route. The goal is to let us perform model swaps with strong per-route SLO-awareness, avoid amplified request queues during swaps, and provide deterministic rollback points. Design highlights: 1) transactional swap plane: introduces a short-lived transactional state where routing changes are prepared, inflight request queues are drained to route-specific holdpoints, and cutover is committed only once safety gates pass; supports abort & rollback to pre-swap pointers. 2) backpressure-smoothing controller: a PID-inspired controller that converts abrupt upstream capacity deltas into smoothed cutover gradients; uses recent queue length, p95 latency delta, and error rate to produce per-route progression rates. 3) progressive cutover anchors: per-route anchors (time + request-count) that define safe checkpoints; the controller uses anchors to hold at safe points and expose them to the Console for manual hold/release. 4) KV cache warmup integration: exposes a lightweight pre-warm handshake to reduce cold-cache request latency on model variants. 5) operator tooling: rwctl commands for previewing swap plans, forcing anchors, and instructing emergency aborts. Testing and validation: unit tests for controller heuristics, e2e scenario tests simulating sudden capacity loss, and a small load test harness that verifies no >10% traffic spikes during a swap. Migration notes: existing route configs continue to work; new swap plane is opt-in via route annotation "rollout.swap=transactional" and defaults to the legacy immediate swap behavior unless enabled. Backward compatibility: routing pointers remain backward-compatible; a safe-mode feature flag can force legacy swap behavior cluster-wide. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated clusters for two weeks, then opt-in for hosted customers with a Console toggle. Related work: ENG-4821 (rollout abstractions) and SUP-1344 (customer incident motivating smoothing).

release_notes: Introduces an opt-in transactional swap mode for model rollouts that smooths backpressure during cutovers, provides per-route anchors for manual inspection and safe rollback, and a rwctl surface for preview/abort operations. Opt-in via route annotation 'rollout.swap=transactional'.
